Read: card 34021 (body and its four comments: claim 6897669560, ruling record 6897685514, correction 6897712329, os-dev-report 6898375321), PR 34052 (body, 45 files, net diff against main e71ecc1b), and the check-runs on this head. The scope is widened to all 13 script files, so the diff has no remainder for a separate ACCEPT. Every check-run on the head is completed, success or skipped; none is red or pending (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests and Governed Surface Queue Guard are success; Check Changeset is skipped, and the PR carries `skip-changeset`).

### ① Derived judgments

1. Seat grammar, widened by one lane word. `l2-review` joins `SEAT_BARE_LANES` (mailbox-open.mjs:204), the signature alternation (check-half-states.mjs:1289, placed before `review`), the hand-off target (record-recognisers.mjs:872) and the seat-title token (fleet-roster.mjs:225). Right: every reader that took `review` now takes both, and the old word still reads everywhere. The slug stays one-to-one: `domain:l2-review` is refused by the reserved set, and no `domain:` name can produce `l2-review-N`.
2. The two words are two seat keys, not one (mailbox-open.mjs:210). Right as a mechanism: folding them would move `mailbox/LOGIN/review-N` and every signature on the board. Wrong in how the rules text describes it: see S1.
3. Two exports removed, `REVIEW_LANE` from fleet-roster.mjs and from check-owed-reviews.mjs. Right: no importer is left anywhere in the tree at this head.
4. Printed text. The Tier S name in check-governed-merges.mjs (1275, 2855) and check-governed-queue-guard.mjs (1600, 1866) equals AGENTS.md:291, and the self-test regexes pin it. The hand-off template equals contract-review.md:22 verbatim, pinned by the self-test. check-owed-reviews prints "L2 seat" while its JSON keys (`reviewSeat`, side `review`) are unchanged. Right.
5. Renames and stubs. `lanes/review.md` to `lanes/l2-review.md` and `review-checklist.md` to `l1-review-checklist.md`, each old path a one-line pointer. check-required-contexts.mjs:650 follows the checklist content to the new path, so the scan does not read the stub. Right. No other file in the tree names the old paths as live paths.
6. Ratchet rows. SKILL.md 320 to 328, the charter 21 to 22 under its new key, the checklist 76 under its new key, two stub rows of 1. Line counts at the head are 328, 22, 76, 1 and 1. Both raises quote ruling record 6897685514 and the measured delta, as card item 5 allows. Right.
7. Three changes of substance, not of wording. area-lease.md:13 drops the account clause (another account sits; the same account needs the maintainer's word) and names the area threads L1. lanes/l2-review.md:20 drops the area-lease exception and says L1 threads are not limited. Both right against card acceptance item 1 (the review lane's account and independence rules belong to L2 only) and the card's Problem section, which names the area's review threads as the ordinary review. The clause on main cited `lanes/review.md` as its source, so it was the L2 seat's rule applied to an L1 thread. The third change is the narrowing in N1.
8. The glossary's tier line (SKILL.md:50) matches contract-review.md:9-11 and the template's face table: schema, governed rules text and a declared narrowing at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; a `Clause-②: yes` declaration alone at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Right.

No published package surface, schema, error code or export changes.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right. The diff is `.claude/**`, one line of `AGENTS.md` and `scripts/**`; no package ships any of it.

Clause-②: no — holds. It is on the PR body and on the claim. No published contract surface is touched, and nothing published is narrowed. The widened accept set in ① is the fleet's own tooling.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Report and head. The os-dev-report on the card covers b49563c6. This head adds a merge of main (584caabb) and one runbook line (661e467b). The record judges the tree at this head; the head's own check-runs are green.
- Open question 1 (keep the AGENTS.md line, which makes the PR Tier H): answered, keep. AGENTS.md is in the card's census surface and line 291 was a bare 复核 that means L2; the three printers move with it. The card's note expected Tier S. Tier H follows from AGENTS.md's own rule, so this record is not enough to land: the authorized approval is still owed, and that approval is where the maintainer answers the question.
- Open question 2 (rename `Reviewed-by:`): answered, keep. The key exists only inside a `## Contract review` record, and card item 3 lists its reader as an identifier that must stay accepted.
- Open question 3 (rename `check-owed-reviews.mjs` and `verify-review-tier.mjs`): answered, follow-up. Both names say only "review" and mean L2, so card item 3 is not met for them at this head. The rules text and the files agree as they stand. The seat owes the follow-up card before `Fixes` closes 34021; whether the card closes with that part open is the L1 ACCEPT's call.
- Deviation, script comments. About 1,100 English "review" lines in `scripts/pm` were not read line by line (declared). Card item 2 is therefore partly met for scripts. N5 names the ones this read found. The same follow-up card carries them.
- Deviation, `scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs` outside `scripts/pm`: right, it is the gate that enforces the renamed checklist.
- Out-of-scope note on check-owed-reviews barring an L2 seat on the PR's own account: at this head the tool and lanes/l2-review.md:20 agree. The disagreement the report describes needs PR 33938, which is not in this tree.
- Landing order. The card's note says this lands after PR 33938. Main at e71ecc1b does not hold 33938 (area-lease.md:13 on main is the old sentence). The merge that brings it rewrites lines in two `hits` files, so it is a substantive head and this record does not cover it.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; nothing written off the relay.
- SQL push-down: no query, id materialisation or join in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

Accepted against the card's two misreads. A PR that touches no face: SKILL.md:48 says every dispatched PR owes L1 and contract-review.md:5 says only a face owes L2, so "no face, no review" no longer reads. A same-account review thread in area-lease mode: area-lease.md:13, SKILL.md:51 and lanes/l2-review.md:20 all say the L2 seat's account rules do not reach an L1 thread. Both misreads are closed.

Census, read on the tree and not from the PR body: every 复核, 复审 and 审核 left without a level tag in `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**`, `.claude/agents/**` and `AGENTS.md` is a plain verb, another review (triage re-grade, security analysis, the director's check, the human approval, GitHub's review) or a verbatim quote, except the two os-dev.md lines in N4. No 达档复核 or 契约复审档 is left in the surface.

Per file:

- `SKILL.md`: the glossary (46-52) carries all four statements card item 1 asks for, at the entry point. L1 is right at 5, 19, 94, 129, 290 and 302 (302 against `h12OrphanLanding`, check-half-states.mjs:3744: ready means ACCEPTed). L2 at 174; both at 34, 67, 247. Findings: S1 (52), N1 (28, 81), N6 (48).
- `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`: 340 is L1 and 352 is L2, both the right level. N4.
- `AGENTS.md`: line 291 agrees with its printers, and the sentence around it defines the term by the record it names.
- `references/contract-review.md`: every 复核 here was the contract-surface step; all now read L2. Line 22 equals the tool's template, line 23 keeps its quote. Lines 8, 14, 18 and 44 are L1 rules that live in this file; they still bind L1 by their own words (ACCEPT, 席位自读). Holds.
- `references/lanes/l2-review.md`: 6 and 9 agree with `seatKey`; 14 and 15 with the claim side and the owed list (both words read); 20 with `isBarred`, which never had the area-lease exception. Holds.
- `references/lanes/review.md` and `references/review-checklist.md` (stubs): each old path resolves to its new file. S1 covers the first stub's wording.
- `references/l1-review-checklist.md`: the old file with three word edits (lines 1, 3, 36), diffed. Holds.
- `references/area-lease.md`: line 13 as in ① item 7, and it names new threads `L1-a` with running threads keeping their names (card item 4). 25, 44, 48 hold. N1 (51), N2 (4).
- `references/execution-duties.md`: the heading 〈L1 审核〉 matches the checklist's pointer. The tier name 契约审核档 is renamed in every place it occurs. Line 135 sends a disputed order to the L1 thread; the L2 seat writes records only, so no other target exists. Holds.
- `references/dispatch-runbook.md`: 44-46, 60, 137, 174, 220 are L2; 193 and 219 L1; 134, 144, 163 both. 219 agrees with execution-duties.md:135. Holds.
- `references/landing-operations.md`: the clause-② gate lines (8, 11-18) are L2; 58, 84, 107 L1; 94 both. Holds.
- `references/coordinator.md`, `cross-repo-coordination.md`, `external-contributions.md`, `filing-gate.md`, `instrument-discipline.md`, `platform-readings.md`, `reading-discipline.md`, `seat-lifecycle.md`, `security-findings.md`, `triage-duties.md`: each changed line read in its sentence; the level is right in each.
- `references/project-forms.md`: line 37 agrees with `MAILBOX_KEYS`. N3 (13).
- `references/lanes/cloud.md`, `hotcrm.md`, `mobile.md`, `ui.md`: the seat's own loop is L1; ui.md:23 is L2. Right. mobile.md:9 is under N1.
- `references/lanes/director.md`, `security.md`, `server.md`, `skills.md`, `spec.md`: L2 where the line meant the contract record, both levels at skills.md 23 and 33. Right.

Implementing files: `mailbox-open.mjs`, `check-half-states.mjs`, `fleet-roster.mjs`, `check-owed-reviews.mjs`, `record-recognisers.mjs` and `post-stamped.mjs` read both lane words exactly as lanes/l2-review.md:6-7 says, and check-owed-reviews takes its seats from `parseSeat`, so the new title parses there too. `check-governed-merges.mjs` and `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` print AGENTS.md:291's name. `check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` and `check-required-contexts.mjs` as in ①. `dispatch-gates.data.mjs`, `dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs` and `ensure-pm-labels.sh` only follow renamed paths and headings. The code agrees with the text, except for S1.

Findings:

S1 (should-fix) — SKILL.md:52 says old seat names are read and never written (旧席名只读不写), and the stub lanes/review.md:1 says new writes use `l2-review#N`. lanes/l2-review.md:7 says a seated seat keeps its original name, and the tools keep the two words as two seat keys (mailbox-open.mjs:210; line 203 says the seated seat keeps its key, slug, mailbox and signature). So a seated `review#N` seat must keep writing `review#N`. fleet-roster.mjs:462 and 472 key a seat's claims and signed activity by the lane word in its seat-post title: a seat that follows SKILL.md:52 and signs `l2-review#N` under a `review` post loses its in-flight and its last activity on the roster, and can read as 疑似撞墙. A lane that follows it and writes `Contract-review-handoff: l2-review#1` or `To: l2-review#1` (post-stamped.mjs:2576 prints that spelling) to the only seated seat, `review#1`, names a seat nobody holds, and check-owed-reviews prints that seat as the taker. The entry-point sentence and the charter line disagree, and SKILL.md's stricter-rule clause picks the one the tools break on. This is the case card item 3 exists for: running threads must not break. Fix: one clause on SKILL.md:52 and on the stub line saying a seated seat keeps and writes its own name, in its signature and in lines addressed to it, and only new seats take `l2-review`. record-recognisers.mjs:1326 already says it correctly.

N1 (nit) — three lines narrow to L1 where the old word covered both steps, against the PR's own rule of writing L1/L2 there: SKILL.md:28 (the red line on merging an unreviewed PR), SKILL.md:81 with lanes/mobile.md:9 (self-retire), and area-lease.md:51 (no rotation mid-review; seat-lifecycle.md:82 says L1/L2 for the same rule). No gate changes: landing-operations.md:8 and contract-review.md:51 still forbid landing without the owed L2.

N2 (nit) — area-lease.md:4 now reads "L1 线程 + 区域 PASS 后自落地". PASS is the L2 record's verdict; the L1 verdict in SKILL.md:48 is ACCEPT. Lines 45-46 state the landing precisely, so nothing depends on the summary.

N3 (nit) — project-forms.md:13 drops the mapping of the seat word 复核 and gives "L2". Only lanes/l2-review.md:7 says 复核 still reads as a seat word, which is the file a coordinator opens after resolving the word.

N4 (nit) — os-dev.md:340 and 352 use L1 and L2, but the glossary is in SKILL.md, which dispatch-runbook.md:143 tells a card thread not to read. os-dev.md:164 and 175 keep a bare 复核; line 175 is the same sentence as l1-review-checklist.md:36, which was tagged L1.

N5 (nit) — script prose behind the text. record-recognisers.mjs:1869 and check-governed-queue-guard.mjs:379 quote the rule as 「复核记录 = 一条评论落 PR 或卡」 and say it is quoted, not paraphrased; contract-review.md:33 now reads 「L2 记录 = …」. check-half-states.mjs:1265 lists the lane words without `l2-review`, one screen above the alternation that accepts it. fleet-roster.mjs:53 still says "A `review` seat". These are script files, so they go to the follow-up card.

N6 (nit) — SKILL.md:48 says L1 reads ACCEPT on a finalized green head (the card's own words). landing-operations.md:59-60 still has ACCEPT first, then the timed wait for the gate jobs, then the flip. Under the stricter-rule clause a seat now waits for green before ACCEPT. Worth one line in the follow-up to make the two say the same thing.

No must-fix. S1 is open on this head and earns a delta review of its fix.

Delta round on record 6899070547 (head 661e467b). Between the two heads: a merge of main up to 86350e12 (5f21a212), the fix commit 3d8db5b7, and a merge of main up to b4eea885 (this head). Read: the card and its four comments (unchanged), the PR body as it now stands, the diff between the two heads, the net diff against main at this head (46 files; merge base b4eea885), and the check-runs on this head. The 54 check-runs are all completed: 32 success, 22 skipped, none red or pending. `hits` grew by one file, `references/lanes/objectstack.md`, which main added and this PR renames two words in. The scope again takes all 13 script files, so the diff has no remainder.

Method: the PR's own changed lines at the old head and at this head were compared line for line. Every difference is one of three kinds: the fix commit, main's new sentences under this PR's names, or a conflict resolution. Each is judged below; lines that did not move keep the judgment of record 6899070547.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Seat grammar, the two seat keys, the removed exports, the printed strings, the renames and stubs, and the glossary's tier line: unchanged between the heads. The judgments of record 6899070547 (① items 1 to 6 and 8) stand.

Line counts at this head are 329, 22 (charter), 76 (L1 checklist), 1 and 1 (stubs). The rows for `area-lease.md` (71) and `lanes/objectstack.md` (35) are main's and untouched. Right.
3. The account rule. Item 7 of the earlier record no longer applies: main now carries the rule itself. `area-lease.md:13` is main's sentence under the new names plus the naming clause for new threads, and `lanes/l2-review.md:20` is main's independence sentence, byte for byte (two sessions differ; the account is not limited). This PR changes no substance there. Right.
4. The fix commit. Three alias sentences (`SKILL.md:52`, `lanes/l2-review.md:7`, the stub `lanes/review.md:1`) now say what the tools do: a seat seated as `review#N` keeps writing its own name, and only new seats take `l2-review`. Three lines read L1/L2 again where the old word covered both steps. Right.
5. Conflict in `record-recognisers.mjs`. The import at line 138 is the union of main's two names and this PR's two. `MAILBOX_KEYS` keeps main's new release-blocker row unchanged (it is not in the net diff); the two contract-review rows carry this PR's wording as before. Right.
6. `check-owed-reviews.mjs`. Main's new area-lease note and its bar are carried under the new names; the behaviour is main's, unchanged. See ③ and N7.

No published package surface, schema, error code or export changes.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged. `skip-changeset` is right: the diff is `.claude/**`, one line of `AGENTS.md` and `scripts/**`, and no package ships any of it.

Clause-②: no — holds, on the PR body and on the claim.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Report and head. The card carries no new dev report for this head. The PR body says what this head does with each finding of the earlier record; the tree was judged, not that account.
- Landing order. The card's note asked that this land after PR 33938. That PR is now in main and in this head, so the condition is met.
- Inherited from main, escalated. `check-owed-reviews.mjs:298-303` bars an L2 seat that sits on the PR's own account and cites the charter's independence section; `:507-509` prints a note about an area-lease exception. At this head `lanes/l2-review.md:20` says the account is not limited, and `area-lease.md` holds no such exception. The same disagreement is on main at b4eea885 between `lanes/review.md:19` and the same tool, so this PR neither creates it nor changes the behaviour; it only renames the words. It is not graded on this head for that reason. It needs a carrier card: the PR body names the card behind PR 33938, and the seat confirms that card exists and is open before ACCEPT. The tool is report-only, and it errs toward naming the lane seat as taker.
- Not taken from the earlier record: N4 and N6, both nits, declared in the PR body. They stand as accepted deviations for the follow-up card.
- The three open questions of the first round keep their answers. The PR is still Tier H through its one `AGENTS.md` line, so the authorized approval is still owed beside this record. The follow-up card for the two script file names is still owed before `Fixes` closes card 34021.
- Main is three commits past the merge base (fa1fb6f4). None of them touches `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md` or `scripts/pm`.

### ④ Design judgment

Findings of record 6899070547:

S1: closed. `SKILL.md:52` now reads that old words and old paths are read and not written, except that a seated `review#N` seat still writes its original name. The stub and the charter line say the same and add the lines addressed to that seat. This agrees with `mailbox-open.mjs:210` (two keys) and `fleet-roster.mjs:462` and `:472` (claims and activity keyed by the title's lane word). No line was added; all three lines are within the 120-byte cap.

N1: closed. `SKILL.md:28` and `:81`, `lanes/mobile.md:9` and `area-lease.md:62` read L1/L2.

N2: closed. `area-lease.md:4` pairs the L1 thread with ACCEPT, which is also the word main's own line 50 uses for that thread's verdict.
